cases.claim: Monster attack specials 1 through 7 and 16 preserve Castle's shared potency-before-save order, exact save and condition identities, permanent-condition sentinel, corrected party starting-duration-under-30 gate, uncapped monster stacking, target-specific sounds, and whole-attack whiff against a monster above 100 magic resistance.

remake.behavior: Remake supplies an explicit eight-special mapping and tests successful saves, permanent traits, the party duration gate, uncapped monster durations, and monster magic resistance. Its helper is a functional lead rather than the authority: when duration is not injected it evaluates the save before rolling duration, unlike Castle's enclosing attack flow.

authoredInputs: monster attack special and damage range
monster hit dice and runtime magic resistance
monster saves, spell immunities, and type flags
castle.observation: After ordinary damage is rolled, every nonzero special consumes randrange(hitDice/2, hitDice), floored at one. Specials 1/2/4/7 use save 5; 3/5 use save 7; and 6/16 use save 4. Failed party saves affect conditions 0/1/5/29, 3/6, and 9/28 respectively only when the current value is nonnegative; the pinned correction adds potency once when the starting value is below 30, even if the result exceeds 30, and still reports the result when the starting value is already 30. Monster targets stack without that gate. Monster save 7 averages six saves; other saves honor their shifted save byte, spell immunity, and undead auto-save after consuming the roll. A monster target above 100 magic resistance jumps to whiff after potency and loses ordinary damage. Party statuses use sound 630; monster disease uses 684 and the other monster statuses use 630.

providence.expectedRepresentation: Schema v2 already preserves each attack row's damageMin, damageMax, and special plus monster hitDice, runtime magicResistance inputs, typeFlags, saves, and spellImmunities; no compiler correction is required.

cases.claim: Monster attack specials 8 and 9 preserve Castle's shared potency-before-save order and mutate the direct Realmz resources: spell drain transfers up to three spell points per attacker hit die without clamping the attacker to its maximum, while experience drain subtracts twenty times attacker maximum stamina from a party character and has no monster-target branch.

remake.behavior: Remake implements both drains in its Classic monster-special dispatcher, including save families, uncapped attacker spell points, and party-only experience drain. Its experience adapter increases Remake's experience-to-next-level balance, whereas 2.0 can mutate Castle's direct earned-experience value.

authoredInputs: monster hit dice and runtime maximum stamina
monster saves, spell immunities, and runtime magic resistance
castle.observation: After ordinary damage and the generic potency draw, special 8 calls savevs(6) before testing the target spell-point balance. Failure transfers min(target spell points, hit dice times three) to the attacker; the attacker is not capped to maxspellpoints and no sound is requested. Party-target special 9 calls savevs(5), subtracts staminamax times twenty from the character's int32 earned experience without a zero floor, requests sound 630, and reports result -18. There is no monster-target case 9 and therefore no save draw there. A monster target above 100 runtime magic resistance reaches whiff before either resource-special save. Ordinary physical damage follows the special when the whole attack did not whiff.

providence.expectedRepresentation: Schema v2 already preserves each attack special, monster hit dice, stamina bonus, spell points, saves, spell immunities, and magic resistance. Runtime maximum stamina remains derived by the fixed MonsterRules construction path; no compiler correction is required.

cases.claim: Monster weapon-to-hit requirements remain distinct from battle placement distance and magical-plus thresholds. Realmz 2.0 intentionally follows Divinity's Item Number contract for specific weapons, preserves the signed-byte representation, and requires a real matching weapon for blunt, sharp, and exact-item restrictions.

remake.behavior: Remake recognized the monster distance byte as a required-weapon field, mapped positive values directly to Classic item identity, kept blunt and sharp sentinels separate, and enforced the resulting metadata before its generic accuracy calculation. It is corroborating implementation evidence rather than the authority.

authoredInputs: Data ID item number and internal itemid
castle.observation: Battle Data BD has a separate distance byte that combatsetup randomizes for initial placement. Monster Data MD dist is the weapon-to-hit byte. Castle correctly checks -1 blunt and -2 sharp for armed attackers, but its armed guard lets all unarmed attacks bypass those restrictions. For a specific item it compares the signed monster byte to item.itemid minus 1024. The shipped Data ID stores ordinary 1..999 item IDs, byte-identically in Castle and Providence, so the comparison cannot satisfy Divinity's documented Item Number contract. The correction fixture records both defects without claiming a Castle runtime observation.

providence.expectedRepresentation: Schema v2 emits monster requiredWeapon and magicToHit separately from battle distance. requiredWeapon retains the exact signed byte; values other than zero, -1, and -2 normalize to the authored unsigned Item Number at the rules boundary.

expectedTrace: explicit typed block or ordinary attack continuation
